ctx.x: So it was a swinging thing, and those guys could play. And he had some great musicians in his band. In fact, a guy that was a great arranger, Jimmy Mundy, oh, man, and he had another trombone player. He had three trombonists -- another guy named Zilch, another guy named Al Wynn. Did you know Al Wynn? He was a real quiet fellow, but he was a very good musician. Of course, he had five saxophones. He had three trombones and three trumpets. He had a trumpet player that doubled on alto sax and

trumpet that I made some things for, and you should know this name, George Dixon. Well, Earl made quite a few records, and George did a lot of the solo work, and, of course, George was what they called, in again, bands in those days, he was the straw boss, you know. He took charge when Earl wasn't around. You know, and this was the nickname they label you with, like in Count Basie's band here a few years back when Marshall Royal was leading the band, they called him the straw boss, you know. So this is the title…
